newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds end off nervy, but trend seen up.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds end off nervy, but trend seen up.

text.p: 1630 GMT - Austrian bonds ended weaker in jittery trade on Thursday, due to profit taking on recent gains but traders said the underlying positive trend remained intact.
A slide in German bunds and U.S. Treasuries on the back of lower-than-expected U.S. jobless claims, indicating a possible rise in inflation, helped to fuel the drop in the Austrian market.
"This is a correction in a bull market," said one trader.
"The market is not a one-way street. We're finally seeing the correction everyone's been expecting," said another.
The nervousness in the market had been tangible after the U.S. tumble, one dealer said. A U.S. employment report out on Friday was expected to provide further stimulus to the market.
* Latest 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 up 10 bps at 101.10 to yield 5.72 (5.73) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.41/51 to yield 5.81/80.
* At the near end, five-year 5.50 percent bond maturing March 2001 up 15 bps at 103.65 to yield 4.59 (4.62) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 103.18/28 to yield 4.70/68 percent.
* 10-year spread to German bunds down one bp at eight, five-year spread steady at 15 bps.
* December AGB future up 28 bps at 108.63 on volume of 702 contracts.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR at 3.350 and overnight money at 3.03/28. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
